item.title: Lawmakers push wave of immigration bills aligned with Trump agenda
item.description: Here's a guide to Indiana’s 2026 immigration bills, including policing, jobs and schools.

item.title: IMPD veteran Tanya Terry is Indianapolis' first female police chief
item.description: Indianapolis Mayor Joe Hogsett appointed Tanya Terry, a 27-year police veteran, as IMPD’s new Chief of Police.

item.title: Ryan Mears announces reelection bid for county prosecutor
item.description: Ryan Mears has taken himself off the short list of potential successors to Mayor Joe Hogsett — at least for now.

item.title: Bill creates in-person checks for Department of Child Services following death of Indianapolis five-year-old
item.description: Lawmakers unanimously moved a bill forward requiring in person checks for the Department of Child Services before they can close out alleged cases of abuse and neglect. The bill is in response to the death of an Indianapolis five-year-old.

item.title: IPS experiences biggest enrollment loss since pandemic, state records show
item.description: Indianapolis Public Schools experienced its greatest annual enrollment decline since the pandemic while charter school enrollment also dropped — trends that could signal fundamental challenges for both school types.

item.title: 'No politics, just keep people alive': Syringe services hope legality continues
item.description: Six Indiana counties operate a syringe service program, often acting as a bridge to healthcare, overdose prevention education and addiction treatment. But the programs could end in July, when the law allowing them expires.

item.title: Indiana National Guard moves closer to expanded policing powers through new legislation
item.description: A bill advancing at the Statehouse would allow Indiana National Guard military police to make arrests and conduct searches when activated by the governor.

item.title: Bill to allow firing squads to carry out death sentences fails House vote
item.description: Lawmakers voted against a bill to allow death sentences to be carried out by firing squads. Many lawmakers indicated they opposed death sentences altogether.

item.title: Martin University's closure brings founder Boniface Hardin's vision for equity to an end
item.description: Last December, Martin University, Indiana’s only predominantly Black college, announced it would close. The school was founded by the late activist and Catholic priest Boniface Hardin, with a mission to serve students historically excluded from higher education.

item.title: Vigil remembers lives lost during immigration enforcement
item.description: The vigil, organized by the Marion County Young Democrats, was for people who have died or disappeared during immigration enforcement.
